# osc_backups (Data Source)

Lists the backups of a database instance, newest first, both scheduled ones and ones taken manually. Use it to find the name of a backup to restore from with the OSC CLI, dashboard or API. Schedule backups with `osc_backup_schedule`.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# The backups of a database, newest first.
data "osc_backups" "db" {
  service_id    = "birme-osc-postgresql"
  instance_name = "mydb"
}

# The newest completed backup, to name in a restore.
output "latest_backup" {
  value = try([for b in data.osc_backups.db.backups : b.name if b.status == "Complete"][0], null)
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `instance_name` (String) Name of the instance.
- `service_id` (String) Service of the instance, one of `birme-osc-postgresql`, `linuxserver-docker-mariadb`, `valkey-io-valkey`, `clickhouse-clickhouse`, `apache-couchdb`, `go-gitea-gitea`.

### Read-Only

- `backups` (Attributes List) The backups, newest first. Empty if the instance has none, or does not exist. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--backups))
- `id` (String) `service_id/instance_name`.

<a id="nestedatt--backups"></a>
### Nested Schema for `backups`

Read-Only:

- `created_at` (String) When the backup was started, in RFC 3339.
- `error` (String) Why the backup failed. Empty unless it did.
- `name` (String) Backup name, which identifies it for a restore.
- `source` (String) `scheduled` or `manual`.
- `status` (String) `Running`, `Complete` or `Failed`. OSC reports some finished backups as `SuccessCriteriaMet` or `FailureTarget`, the Kubernetes job conditions that precede the final one; they are shown as `Complete` and `Failed`.
